    "title": "OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot paginate the datetime field used by audit logs",
    "body": "OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does `int(math.floor(value) if self._is_asc(for_prev) else math.ceil(value))`, but OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint constructs it with `order_by=\"-datetime\"`. For AuditLogEntry rows, `getattr(item, self.key)` is a datetime, and `math.floor`/`math.ceil` cannot convert a datetime to a number, so even the first page raises TypeError inside build_cursor. Any admin request with `optimized_pagination=true` will return HTTP 500. Additionally, value_from_cursor returns the raw integer cursor value instead of converting it back to a datetime for build_queryset, so subsequent pages would also be broken. The paginator must either be restricted to numeric keys or implement DateTimePaginator-style epoch conversion and reverse conversion."

    "body": "When `enable_advanced_features` is true and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code sets `start_offset = cursor.offset` (negative) and then evaluates `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative offsets and raises an exception. A privileged user can trigger this with a crafted cursor such as `cursor=0:-1:0` plus `optimized_pagination=true`, causing an unhandled 500. Offset should be validated as non-negative before building the slice."

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot paginate the datetime field used by audit logs
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does `int(math.floor(value) if self._is_asc(for_prev) else math.ceil(value))`, but OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint constructs it with `order_by="-datetime"`. For AuditLogEntry rows, `getattr(item, self.key)` is a datetime, and `math.floor`/`math.ceil` cannot convert a datetime to a number, so even the first page raises TypeError inside build_cursor. Any admin request with `optimized_pagination=true` will return HTTP 500. Additionally, value_from_cursor returns the raw integer cursor value instead of converting it back to a datetime for build_queryset, so subsequent pages would also be broken. The paginator must either be restricted to numeric keys or implement DateTimePaginator-style epoch conversion and reverse conversion.

findings.title: Negative offset path passes a negative slice start to Django QuerySet
findings.body: When `enable_advanced_features` is true and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code sets `start_offset = cursor.offset` (negative) and then evaluates `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative offsets and raises an exception. A privileged user can trigger this with a crafted cursor such as `cursor=0:-1:0` plus `optimized_pagination=true`, causing an unhandled 500. Offset should be validated as non-negative before building the slice.

findings.title: No tests cover OptimizedCursorPaginator or the new endpoint flag
findings.body: The PR adds a new paginator class and a new `optimized_pagination` request path but no tests. A basic test for the first page with `order_by="-datetime"` would catch the datetime conversion crash, and a crafted negative-offset cursor test would catch the negative slicing crash. Add paginator unit tests and endpoint tests for both the enabled and fallback paths.

findings.title: Misleading comment about negative offset support
findings.body: The added comment says the change allows negative offsets for advanced pagination scenarios, but `self.offset = int(offset)` already accepted negative integers and this file adds no negative-aware behavior or validation. The comment describes behavior that is not implemented here and may mislead maintainers into believing negative offsets are safely supported.
